findings.root_cause: Migration DDL and ORM model disagree on the pharmacy primary-key type; never detected because upgrade head could not run at all (NR-002 masked it).
findings.evidence:
psycopg2.errors.DatatypeMismatch: Key columns 'original_drug_catalog_id' and 'id' are of incompatible types: character varying and integer (local run and CI job 102182712083). Counts: 23 Integer-id creates vs 28 ULID ORM classes.

[2026-09-25 addendum, executed independently] Reproduction matches the authorised exception record exactly: 94 of 101 revisions log `Running upgrade`, the failure is psycopg2.errors.DatatypeMismatch on constraint pharmacy_drug_substitution_rules_original_drug_catalog_id_fkey, and alembic_version reads 20260505_0005 with 32 tables. Graph facts, computed: one root, ONE head (20260908_0001), 4 merge revisions, 5 branch points — so this is NOT head divergence. 20260716_0003 (the only creator of pharmacy_drug_catalog, id = Integer) IS an ancestor of 20260815_0023, so the migration is unconditionally impossible. Three sources disagree about one column: the creating migration says Integer, every physical database says integer, the ORM says String(26). 20260815_0022 survived the same assumption only because it declared drug_catalog_id String(26) with NO ForeignKey. CLASSIFICATION: canonical identity divergence surfacing as an unsatisfiable FK datatype in a historical migration no database can have applied. The repair on claude/nr-003-canonical-drug-identity was VERIFIED to work here: it takes the fresh upgrade from 94 to 98 revisions, and `upgrade 20260819_0003` then reaches 410 tables, exit 0. findings.root_cause: A tenant-blind service constructor (db, event_bus) combined with a read-modify-write terminal transition and an unconditional device side effect.
findings.evidence:
PRE-FIX, real PostgreSQL, through the real service class: (A) lab A completed lab B's work order — device 'available', order 'completed'. (B) device 'available' while 1 work order still open. (C) two barrier-released threads both returned 'committed'; cost_total=100.0 with T2's 999.0 lost; version stayed 1.
POST-FIX, same database: (A) WorkOrderNotFoundError, lab B's row untouched at 'in_progress'. (B) device stays 'out_of_service' with 1 fault open, and is released only when the last one closes. (C) exactly one commit, one WorkOrderAlreadyClosedError, version 1 -> 2.

findings.status: FIXED — VERIFIED (real PostgreSQL, pre-fix reproduced and post-fix proved)
findings.title: Completing one work order returned a still-faulty device to clinical service, across any tenant, any number of times
findings.description:
BiomedicalService.complete_work_order carried three defects on a LIVE, migration-backed table (biomed_work_orders) reachable at POST /biomedical/work-orders/{wo_id}/complete.

(1) The lookup was filter_by(id=wo_id) with no tenant predicate, and the service had no tenant context at all to scope it with. A caller acting for lab A completed lab B's work order and flipped lab B's device to available. The router requires system:admin, but admin is a lab-scoped role here — only master_admin and ministry_admin are cross-tenant — so this was a genuine cross-tenant mutation, not an intended override.

(2) Closing ANY work order set device.status = AVAILABLE unconditionally. A class III ventilator held out_of_service with two open work orders became available when only the first was completed; the second fault was never touched. Returning a device to clinical service is a safety decision, and closing one ticket says nothing about the faults the other tickets were raised for.

(3) No row lock and no terminal-state guard: two concurrent transactions both committed the same terminal transition, the later write silently replaced the earlier one's cost and action record, and `version` never moved off 1 although the model carries the optimistic-lock column.

findings.title: 28 mutating service methods select a row by id with no tenant predicate anywhere in the method
findings.description:
The defect fixed in NR-016 is an instance of a pattern, not a one-off. An AST pass over backend/app found 28 mutating methods (they set .status, commit, or delete) whose row lookup is filter_by(id=...) and which contain no lab_id or tenant reference anywhere in the method body.

By domain: blood_bank 5, critical_care 4, lifecycle_platform 4, national/notification_platform 4, biomedical 3, command_center 2, document_intelligence 2, ems 2, pilot_platform 1, public_health 1.

A second pass split them by whether the method name is called from any api/routes module: 24 apparently route-reachable, 4 not.

CAVEAT, stated because it changes what this number means. The reachability test matches on method NAME, so generic names over-count: the four notification_platform save()/delete() hits and the two document_intelligence delete()/unregister() hits are very likely matching an unrelated class. Treat 24 as an upper bound, not a count of confirmed live holes. Only NR-016 was individually traced end to end and reproduced.

THE 4 NOT ROUTE-REACHABLE ARE INFORMATIVE. blood_bank start_transfusion() and complete_transfusion() are tenant-blind but SUPERSEDED: the routes call start_transfusion_safely() and complete_transfusion_safely(transfusion_id, lab_id, body), which do take the tenant. So the earlier blood-bank hardening left the unscoped originals in place rather than removing them. They are dead weight that reads like a live hole and would become one if anything called them again.

TRACED 2026-09-25, and the heuristic's over-count is now demonstrated twice:
  critical_care.discharge_patient() — SAFE / DEAD-SUPERSEDED. The route calls discharge_patient_safely(admission_id, body, lab_id), which has the lab filter, .with_for_update(), is_deleted, a terminal-state guard over {discharged, transferred, deceased}, required-field validation, version += 1 and a bed lock with an ownership check — wrapped by ClinicalCommandGuard with If-Match and an idempotency key. It is the reference implementation in this codebase. My earlier scan matched it only because app/nhdw/routes.py calls an unrelated NHDWService.discharge_patient.
  command_center.resolve_emergency() + fulfill_resource() — REAL LIVE DEFECTS, reproduced on real PostgreSQL and fixed. See NR-021.

So of the 3 candidates individually traced so far (biomedical, critical_care, command_center), 1 was safe and 2 were real. The remaining ~21 must each be traced the same way; the count is not evidence.

findings.title: Every adaptive-auth endpoint taking account_id binds the caller zero times (IDOR)
findings.description:
app/identity/adaptive_auth/routes.py has 16 handlers; 7 take an `account_id` from the path or query, and NONE of them binds it to the authenticated caller. The router applies _AUTH_REQUIRED, so a caller must be authenticated — but nothing ties the account being acted on to the account doing the acting.

Measured by AST: handlers=16, taking account_id=7, binding the caller=0.
  get_risk_history        — read ANY account's security risk events
  list_travel_events      — read ANY account's impossible-travel records, i.e. physical location history
  get_active_session_count— read ANY account's live session count
  create_mfa_challenge    — MINT AN MFA CHALLENGE AGAINST ANY ACCOUNT (a write into another subject's authentication flow, not merely a read)
  evaluate_risk, detect_new_device, enforce_session_policy — writes against any account

create_mfa_challenge and the location-history disclosure are why this is P0 rather than P1.

Which capability authorises reading and writing another subject's adaptive-auth state, and does create_mfa_challenge become self-only? Inventing that authorisation model unilaterally is exactly what this brief forbids, so it is recorded instead.

findings.root_cause: Three of the 25 rules measure something other than what they claim. Rule 10 shells out to flake8 with its DEFAULT line limit of 79, while the repository declares line-length = 100 in pyproject.toml, so every file in the platform that conforms to the project's own standard is reported as violating it. Rule 15 looks for functions never called by name in source, which every FastAPI route handler is by construction, because the decorator registers them. Rule 5 normalises short lines before comparing, so 'from __future__ import annotations', a blank line, a lone ')' and 'try:' count as duplicated code blocks between any two sibling modules changed together. Rule 12 is an aggregate of the other rules and fails whenever they do.
findings.evidence:
Executed locally on 2026-09-25 against head 288b57fe, diff-mode base origin/main, 12 changed files / 9 Python files: compliance score 74.0/100, PASS 16, WARN 5, FAIL 4, exit 1. Per-rule, by invoking each rule function directly (the runner deliberately omits rule identifiers from its own output):
rule5 FAIL — 28 'duplicate blocks'. The first five are biomedical/api/routes.py:1 vs command_center/api/routes.py:1 ('from __future__ import annotations'), :2 vs :2 (blank), :13 vs :20 (')'), :26 vs :33 ('try:'), and service.py:3 vs :4 ('from datetime import datetime, timedelta').
rule10 FAIL — 207 flake8 E501 findings at the 79-character default. Measured at the repository's declared limit of 100, the seven touched files produce 9/30/0/0/6/10/0 findings, and main's copies of the same seven files produce 9/30/0/0/6/10/0 — identical. This change introduces zero new violations of the project's own standard.
rule15 FAIL — 116 'potentially unused' functions, the first ten of which are complete_work_order, create_work_order, get_device, get_dashboard, health and other decorated route handlers in biomedical/api/routes.py.
rule11 architecture score, rule14 architecture violations and rule19 circular dependencies all PASS.

findings.contradictions: The enforcer's rule 10 measures 79 characters; pyproject.toml declares line-length = 100. Both are in the same repository and they disagree.

findings.root_cause: critical_care_infusions is created by 20260716_0007, and verified_by / verified_at are added later by 20260820_0005. That revision is reachable only through head (20260908_0001, a merge of 20260819_0004, 20260820_0005 and 20260908_0002), and head cannot be applied because it fails earlier at NR-003. The only revision that currently applies, 20260908_0002, does not have 20260820_0005 in its ancestry. The route's opening statement is a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE of every ORM column, so the absence raises before the guard, the version check, the tenant predicate or the clinical rule is reached.
findings.evidence:
Executed on PostgreSQL 16.13, schema from `alembic upgrade 20260908_0002` (exit 0, 391 tables). POST /critical-care/infusions/{id}/verify -> HTTP 500 INTERNAL_ERROR; server log: (psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn) column critical_care_infusions.verified_by does not exist, on the FOR UPDATE select. Committed state unchanged (awaiting_verification, version 1). Zero clinical_command_receipts rows, zero audit_logs rows. Graph read programmatically: 20260820_0005 in ancestors(head) = True, in ancestors(20260908_0002) = False. On a fresh `upgrade head` the stamped revision reaches only 20260505_0005 and critical_care_infusions is never created. NEGATIVE PROOF on a disposable database: adding the two columns makes the operation return 200 with awaiting_verification -> active, verified_by set, version 1->2, one completed receipt and one audit row, and makes all six tripwire tests fail; dropping them restores the defect and the suite returns to 25 passed.

[2026-09-25 addendum, executed] Two corrections to this entry's own account. (1) The columns are not merely 'on a branch only head reaches': 20260815_0023 IS an ancestor of 20260820_0005, so the ICU columns are strictly downstream of NR-003 and no ordering reaches them without it. (2) NR-003 is not the only blocker — NR-028 sits directly in front, at 20260820_0004, the direct parent of 20260820_0005. PROVEN COMPLETE: with NR-003's authorised repair applied and the 13 hospital tables probe-created, `upgrade head` completes (exit 0, stamped 20260909_0001, single head, 432 tables), verified_by and verified_at exist, and the full ICU matrix passes on that migration-built critical_care schema — 200 happy path, 409 replay, 422 independence, 404 cross-tenant, 409/428/400 preconditions, [200,409] under a two-actor race, 1 receipt, audit rows present, downgrade/re-upgrade clean. Status for the operation is therefore VERIFIED CONDITIONAL on NR-003 landing and NR-028 closing, and must not be shortened to VERIFIED while either is open.
findings.affected_users: Every ICU clinician; every patient on a high-alert infusion (insulin, heparin, norepinephrine, epinephrine, potassium chloride, propofol, fentanyl, midazolam).
findings.clinical_impact: The independent second-actor check on a high-alert infusion — the control that stops one clinician acting alone on a vasopressor or insulin drip — returns 500 and cannot be completed. Proven on norepinephrine.
findings.security_impact: Tenant isolation on this endpoint becomes unprovable: a cross-tenant attempt returns 500 rather than 404, because the statement carrying the lab_id filter is the statement that raises.
findings.data_integrity_impact: None observed: the transaction rolls back and no partial state is committed.
findings.operational_impact: Four in-handler controls (tenant, stale version, absent version, absent idempotency key) are masked into one opaque 500.

findings.root_cause: Two compounding causes. guard.claim runs after the resource is loaded, so a failure before that point produces no durable claim. And the route's except branch calls guard.reject, which writes to the same database that just refused the statement — the failure path shares its dependency with the thing it is guarding, so the rejection is lost too.
findings.evidence: Executed, PostgreSQL 16.13: POST /critical-care/infusions/{id}/verify returned 500 and both clinical_command_receipts and audit_logs gained zero rows. Asserted as a delta against a baseline captured at fixture setup, not as an absolute zero, so it cannot pass on an unused database. Under the repaired schema the same operation writes one audit row for a success and two for a concurrent success-plus-refusal, which shows the audit path itself is sound and that only the failure path is unrecorded.
findings.affected_components: app/clinical/command_guard.py (reject), every route in the 8 guarded domains
findings.affected_users: Anyone reconstructing a clinical incident.
findings.clinical_impact: Repeated failing attempts to activate a vasopressor infusion leave no evidence that anything was attempted.
findings.security_impact: An attacker probing a guarded clinical endpoint leaves no audit trail when the probe errors.
findings.legal_impact: A regulated clinical action cannot be shown to have been attempted and refused.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: A durable fallback for the case where the database is the failure — structured log, metric, or outbox — so the attempt is recorded even when guard.reject cannot commit. clinical_safety_metrics.record_audit_failure already exists for the audit-write case and is the natural seam.
findings.verification_method: Provoke a failure at each failure_injection stage and assert exactly one durable record of the attempt, with no partial clinical effect.
findings.regression_risk: Low if additive. Must not weaken guard.reject or swallow the exception.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG — REAL_HTTP_POSTGRES at canonical head with a positive control isolating (a) from (b).
findings.status: OPEN — VERIFIED DEFECT by execution. | ADDENDUM 2026-09-25 (canonical lineage efcc4b6e): NARROWED by execution. A refused ICU verification IS audited — clinical.icu.infusion.verify.rejected, naming actor, infusion, state_before and the clinical reason. The original measurement was taken when the DATABASE ITSELF was the failure (UndefinedColumn), so guard.reject shared the broken dependency it was trying to record. That narrower statement stands and is still a real gap; the blanket claim does not. | ADDENDUM 2 (2026-09-25, canonical head): ROOT-CAUSED and SPLIT. The shared-dependency theory is wrong for the case originally measured. Two distinct mechanisms: (a) six blood bank commands have NO guard.reject at all, so nothing can be recorded — now NR-033; (b) on routes that DO call reject, the fallback fires but is an IN-MEMORY per-worker counter (app/clinical/observability.py), and reject() re-raises, so the audit failure MASKS the clinical reason the command was refused for (FM-026, executed for the first time). log_action does flush inside the try/except, so the except branch is reachable — it simply is never called in (a).
findings.title: A protected clinical command that fails writes no receipt and no audit row

So the classification is MIGRATION_BLOCKED, not schema drift: the columns exist in the corpus and are unreachable, exactly like NR-023's. The runtime question — whether lockout is enforced and survives a restart — remains UNKNOWN; it was still not executed.

findings.security_impact: Either the brute-force lockout control is inoperative, or any code path that writes it raises. Both are serious and they are different defects; no HTTP authentication attempt was executed here, so the register does not choose between them.

findings.evidence_strength: STRONG — REAL_HTTP_POSTGRES at canonical head, 6 tests, negative-proofed: clearing locked_until makes the same password return 200 with a JWT, so the 401 is caused by the lock and nothing else.
findings.status: RESOLVED — VERIFIED by execution. The columns exist on a database built only by migrations at canonical head, and the control is live and correct: 5 failed logins set the deadline, the correct password is refused while the window is open, the refusal is indistinguishable from a wrong password, expiry restores access and resets the counter, and the lock survives a real PostgreSQL restart. findings.root_cause: `alembic upgrade head` fails on an empty database at 20260505_0005 (NR-003, pharmacy original_drug_catalog_id varchar against id integer). The furthest revision that applies is 20260908_0002, which excludes several branches. Every ORM model whose table or columns arrive on an excluded branch therefore describes a schema no operator can build.
findings.evidence:
Executed, PostgreSQL 16.13. 781 mapped ORM classes; 391 physical tables; 405 mapped tables with no physical table at all; 84 tables with column drift totalling 692 columns. By prefix: pharmacy 23, radiology 17, nhdw 14, nursing 13, ecosystem 3, fin 3, gov 3, plus clinical, critical_care, lab_users, national, niam, organizations, service_accounts, users. Three of the eight ClinicalCommandGuard-protected domains drift on their core table: critical_care_infusions (2), pharmacy_prescriptions (15), radiology_orders (7).

[2026-09-25 addendum, executed] Re-measured on a head-built database (20260909_0001, 432 tables): mapped tables absent falls 405 -> 364, tables with drift 84 -> 83, missing columns 692 -> 691. Five of the six divergences pinned as critical are CLEAN at head (critical_care_infusions, lab_users, users, service_accounts, clinical_lab_facility_bindings) and are reclassified MIGRATION_BLOCKED. `organizations` still drifts by 4 columns and is genuine SCHEMA_DRIFT. So reaching head fixes the reachability class but leaves 83 tables / 691 columns of real drift, dominated by pharmacy 27, radiology 17, nhdw 14 and nursing 13. INTENTIONAL and DORMANT are recorded as zero ESTABLISHED, not zero existing: separating deliberate divergence from accidental needs each domain owner.
findings.affected_users: Any fresh deployment, and every clinician in the affected domains.
findings.clinical_impact: Pharmacy and radiology clinical write paths are in the same position as the ICU one proven in NR-023.
findings.operational_impact: The 2733-test suite cannot see any of this: conftest.py hard-assigns DATABASE_URL to sqlite:///:memory: and builds the schema from the ORM, where this class of divergence cannot exist by construction.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Resolve NR-003 so head applies, then re-run the drift report and expect zero. Fixing individual columns branch by branch would multiply the problem.
findings.verification_method: backend/tests/verification/test_schema_drift_guard.py — a ratchet on the count, a zero-tolerance rule on guarded clinical tables, and a refusal to run against a create_all database.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG. Every number produced by a script against a migration-built database, reproducible in under 2 seconds.
findings.status: OPEN — MEASURED. This is NR-003's blast radius, quantified; it is not a separate root cause.
findings.title: On the only applicable build, 405 mapped tables do not exist and 84 more are missing 692 columns

findings.root_cause: 20260820_0004_surgical_safety_checklists.py creates hospital_surgical_safety_checklists with foreign keys to hospital_operation_theaters, hospitals and hospital_departments. No migration in the 101-revision corpus creates any hospital table. The revision therefore aborts inside itself on every migration-built database, and because the abort is internal, nothing ordered after it runs — including 20260820_0005, its direct child, which adds the ICU independent-verification columns. Same authoring pattern as NR-003 one step further: written against a create_all schema where the referenced tables exist because the ORM made them.
findings.evidence: Executed. On claude/nr-003-canonical-drug-identity (which fixes NR-003), a fresh `alembic upgrade head` applies 98 revisions and then fails: psycopg2.errors.UndefinedTable: relation "hospital_operation_theaters" does not exist, on CREATE TABLE hospital_surgical_safety_checklists. Checked against three independently built databases — a 20260908_0002 build (391 tables), a 20260819_0003 build (410 tables) and the failed upgrade head (32 tables): zero hospital* tables in any. Of the 13 ORM tables starting 'hospital', only 3 names appear anywhere in the migration corpus and all 3 only as FK targets or as the one table 0004 creates; 10 are absent entirely. PROOF THAT THIS IS THE LAST BLOCKER: probe-creating the 13 tables from the ORM in FK order on a disposable database, then dropping only the one 0004 creates, lets `upgrade head` complete — exit 0, stamped 20260909_0001, single head, 432 tables — and critical_care_infusions.verified_by and verified_at then exist.
findings.affected_components: migrations/versions/20260820_0004_surgical_safety_checklists.py, app/hospital/models.py (13 tables), the entire path to 20260820_0005 and head
findings.affected_users: Every ICU clinician (NR-023 is downstream of this); every hospital-management user.
findings.clinical_impact: This is the immediate blocker in front of the ICU high-alert infusion second-actor check. It also means the surgical safety checklist — a WHO patient-safety instrument — has no table on any deployable database.
findings.data_integrity_impact: None directly: the transaction rolls back. But a failed upgrade is partially committed at the 20260505_0005 autocommit boundary, so the database is left in a mixed state rather than clean.
findings.operational_impact: alembic upgrade head cannot succeed, so the deployment gate cannot pass, so no CI lane can certify the platform.

findings.verification_method: backend/tests/migrations/test_migration_corpus_completeness.py — static, database-free, catches any FK target the corpus never creates. Then a fresh `upgrade head` to exit 0 with no probe-created tables.
findings.regression_risk: None from recording. The fix creates 13 tables and needs schema-change approval.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG. Reproduced on a fresh database, cross-checked against three builds, and the full chain proven complete by probe: with this and NR-003 satisfied, head applies and the ICU columns exist.

findings.title: The entire hospital domain — 13 ORM tables — has no migrations, and a revision on the ICU path references it

findings.root_cause: CLAUDE.md states as MANDATORY that every migration must be idempotent, using _has_column / _table_exists / _index_exists guards. 20260820_0004 and 20260820_0005 have no guard of any kind: 0004 calls op.create_table unconditionally and 0005 calls op.add_column twice unconditionally. 37 of 101 revisions are in the same position; these two matter most because they are the last two before head on the path NR-023 depends on.
findings.evidence: Executed: after probe-creating the hospital tables, re-running `upgrade head` failed with psycopg2.errors.DuplicateTable on hospital_surgical_safety_checklists — the revision could not be re-run over its own partial effect. Static measurement: 37 of 101 revisions perform op.create_table / add_column / create_index / create_unique_constraint with no recognisable guard. By contrast 20260815_0023, the NR-003 revision, is guarded, and that guard is what made its repair verifiable.
findings.operational_impact: A partial upgrade that stops between these revisions needs a database-level repair rather than a re-run. Given the autocommit boundary at 20260505_0005, partial upgrades are the normal failure mode, not an edge case.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Add the repository's standard guards to the two named revisions. Adding them changes no schema and no ordering, so it is the cheapest item in this cluster. The remaining 35 are pre-existing debt, ratcheted rather than pinned.
findings.verification_method: backend/tests/migrations/test_migration_corpus_completeness.py holds the unguarded count at the measured 37 and pins the two named revisions.
findings.regression_risk: Low. A guard makes a revision skip work already done; it cannot make it do more.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG for both the executed DuplicateTable and the static count.
findings.status: OPEN — MEASURED. Two named revisions have a proven consequence; 37 of 101 lack a guard overall.
findings.title: The two revisions in front of head on the ICU path are not idempotent, so a partial upgrade cannot be resumed

findings.root_cause: routes/login.py calls log_action(...) with user_id and user_role but no lab_id, even in the branches where the LabUser — and therefore its lab — is already resolved.
findings.evidence: POSTGRESQL at canonical head: selecting lab_id for actions LIKE 'login%' returns 18 rows, every one with lab_id NULL. Pinned by test_authentication_audit_rows_are_not_tenant_scoped, which fails if this changes in either direction.
findings.clinical_impact: None directly.
findings.security_impact: A lab administrator querying their own tenant's audit trail sees no authentication events for their own staff, and any per-tenant brute-force or failed-login report keyed on lab_id reads as silence. The events are not lost — they are unattributable by tenant.
findings.data_integrity_impact: None. No row is missing; a column is unset.
findings.operational_impact: Per-tenant security monitoring of authentication is not possible as built.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide the intended scope first. If authentication events are platform-level, record that as the contract and document that tenant audit queries join through user_id. If they should be tenant-scoped, set lab_id in the branches where the LabUser is already resolved — but not where the identifier matched nothing, since inventing a lab_id there would be a guess.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: None applied. This is a classification decision, not a patch.
findings.verification_method: backend/tests/verification/test_account_lockout.py::test_authentication_audit_rows_are_not_tenant_scoped
findings.acceptance_criteria: The intended scope is recorded, and the pinned test matches it.
findings.regression_risk: Low. The pinned test fails loudly if the behaviour changes either way.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG — executed against real PostgreSQL, and pinned by a test.
findings.status: OPEN — MEASURED, classification required. Deliberately not called a defect: authentication precedes workspace resolution, so a platform-level event is defensible. What is not defensible is not knowing which it is.
findings.title: Authentication audit rows are not tenant-scoped (lab_id IS NULL)
findings.description: Every login audit row — login, login_failed, login_lockout_started, login_denied_lockout — is written with lab_id NULL, although the row does carry user_id and user_role. Measured on real PostgreSQL at canonical head while proving NR-025.

findings.root_cause: ORM attributes were not reconciled to the physical pharmacy schema after the catalog identity was settled on an integer primary key (NR-003 / ADR-006).
findings.evidence: POSTGRESQL + STATIC on efcc4b6e (claude/p0-1-hospital-migrations), PostgreSQL 16 at canonical head 20260909_0001. pg_constraint shows the PK integer and all 18 referencing FK columns integer->integer. SQLAlchemy metadata over every loaded class shows 10 declared VARCHAR(26) FKs onto that integer PK.
findings.affected_components: app/pharmacy/models.py (10 classes), any pharmacy write path using them
findings.clinical_impact: Pharmacy inventory, dispensing, prescription items, recalls and waste paths are affected. Not measured end to end here — the ICU proof established only that critical_care is untouched.
findings.security_impact: None identified.
findings.data_integrity_impact: A write through these attributes cannot satisfy the integer FK, so it either raises or targets a column that does not exist.
findings.operational_impact: Pharmacy verification work is blocked until the ORM is reconciled.
findings.recommended_fix: Reconcile the 10 ORM attributes to the physical columns — name drug_id, type Integer — the way the Generation-B pharmacy models were already reconciled. Do not add a migration: the database is already correct.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: None applied. ORM reconciliation across 10 classes needs its own verified pass.
findings.verification_method: Re-run the end-to-end FK type check on canonical head, then exercise one pharmacy write path per affected class against real PostgreSQL.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Zero non-integer ORM FKs onto pharmacy_drug_catalog.id, and one proven write path per class.
findings.regression_risk: Medium — 10 classes, several with live service callers.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG — executed on real PostgreSQL at canonical head.
findings.status: OPEN — VERIFIED DEFECT by execution. Not a migration defect: the migrations produce the correct integer columns. No migration was created.
findings.title: Ten live pharmacy ORM classes declare drug_catalog_id VARCHAR(26) onto an integer catalog PK
findings.description: app.pharmacy.models declares a drug_catalog_id column as VARCHAR(26) with a ForeignKey to pharmacy_drug_catalog.id on DrugBatch, DrugReturn, InventoryForecast, InventoryTransferItem, PrescriptionItem, Recall, PharmacySaleLine, StockLevel, StockMovement and WasteRecord. The physical columns are named drug_id and are integer, so these attributes are both mistyped and misnamed relative to the schema.

findings.root_cause: Type mismatch between audit_logs.resource_id (integer) and string-keyed clinical primary keys.
findings.evidence: POSTGRESQL on efcc4b6e (claude/p0-1-hospital-migrations), PostgreSQL 16 at canonical head 20260909_0001: information_schema gives audit_logs.resource_id = integer and 13 critical_care_* tables with character varying id. Every clinical.icu.infusion.verify row has resource_id NULL and details.resource_id = the infusion id. Pinned by test_17 and test_12.
findings.affected_components: app/clinical/command_guard.py (_audit_resource_id), audit_logs, all 8 guarded domains with string keys
findings.clinical_impact: A safety review cannot query the audit trail by the resource it is investigating; the obvious query returns silence rather than an error. The evidence is not lost — it requires JSON extraction to reach.
findings.security_impact: Weakens audit queryability, not audit integrity. The hash chain and append-only trigger are unaffected.
findings.data_integrity_impact: None. No row is missing and no value is lost; one indexed column is unset.
findings.operational_impact: Per-resource audit reporting for clinical commands needs a JSON path rather than an index.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide the contract. Either widen audit_logs.resource_id to text or add a resource_key text column and populate it, or accept details.resource_id as canonical and document that clinical audit queries use it. Either way a schema change needs human approval per CLAUDE.md.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: None applied. Pinned by a test so a change in either direction surfaces.
findings.verification_method: backend/tests/verification/test_icu_final_proof.py::test_17_clinical_audit_rows_cannot_use_the_indexed_resource_id_column
findings.acceptance_criteria: The intended contract is recorded, and the pin matches it.
findings.regression_risk: Low while pinned.
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG — executed on real PostgreSQL at canonical head, and pinned.
findings.status: OPEN — VERIFIED DEFECT by execution. A deliberate compensation, not a slip: the identity is preserved in details.resource_id. Fixing the column is a schema change, so not applied.
findings.title: Clinical audit rows cannot use the indexed resource_id column (integer vs string keys)
findings.description: audit_logs.resource_id is integer while all 13 critical_care_* tables have character varying primary keys. ClinicalCommandGuard._audit_resource_id therefore returns None for a non-numeric id and writes the real value into the details JSON. Every clinical audit row — success and rejection — has resource_id NULL.

findings.root_cause: The rejection path was never written for these six handlers. The other 30 guarded commands, including all eight ICU commands, do call guard.reject.
findings.evidence: REAL_HTTP_POSTGRES on canonical head 20260909_0001. Injecting a failure at after_business_effect on POST /blood-bank/reservations yields: 0 rejection audit rows, 0 receipts, 0 clinical effect, and 0 audit-failure metric increments. A POSITIVE CONTROL on the ICU verify route — which does call reject — under the same conditions DOES increment the counter, which isolates the cause to the missing path rather than a broken fallback. Pinned by tests/verification/test_guard_reject_coverage.py (static, negative-proofed three ways).
findings.clinical_impact: A refused blood reservation, release, sample, transfusion reaction, return or discard leaves no record of the attempt or the reason. For a transfusion reaction in particular, the refusal of the record is itself clinically significant and is not reconstructable afterwards.
findings.security_impact: Repeated refused attempts against blood inventory are invisible to review.
findings.data_integrity_impact: None — the rollback is clean; no partial effect survives.
findings.operational_impact: Incident reconstruction for these six operations is not possible.
findings.recommended_fix: Add guard.reject to each of the six handlers, mirroring the ICU pattern (rollback, reject with the clinical reason, commit, then raise the mapped error). Doing so changes the response for a refused command, so the clinical owner confirms the intended status codes first.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: None applied. Pinned by a ratchet so a seventh cannot appear silently.
findings.verification_method: tests/verification/test_clinical_failure_trace.py (PostgreSQL) and tests/verification/test_guard_reject_coverage.py (static ratchet)
findings.acceptance_criteria: Each of the six records a rejection row naming actor, resource and reason; the ratchet baseline is emptied deliberately and the failure-trace evidence is re-run.
findings.regression_risk: Medium — six handlers, and the refused-command response shape changes.
findings.owner: Blood Bank clinical owner + Clinical platform
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG — executed on real PostgreSQL with a positive control, and ratcheted.
findings.status: OPEN — VERIFIED DEFECT by execution, root-caused. Not fixed: adding a rejection path changes what a refused clinical command returns, which is a clinical response contract, not a patch.
findings.title: Six guarded blood bank commands have no guard.reject, so a refused command records no reason
findings.description: An AST census over all 36 ClinicalCommandGuard-protected commands finds six whose handler never calls guard.reject: blood.reservation.create, blood.reservation.release, blood.sample.create, blood.reaction.create, blood.return.create and blood.discard.create. All six are in app/blood_bank/api/routes.py. Their except branch is 'db.rollback(); _raise_blood_error(exc); raise' — it rolls back and re-raises without recording anything.
